title: The tool audit credits a test only for code pytest really runs: real hook names, no bare-name collisions, helpers handed on by name
requested_outcome:
The tool audit (experience/tool_matrix.py, `_calls_that_run`) decides which code in a test file runs, and only a tool dispatched from running code is cited as tested. PR #83 (landing commit e701a090) left three edge cases named and unfixed, and all three are still on trunk a68536c6:
- A helper whose name merely starts with setup or teardown is taken for a pytest hook and credited without being called: `_HOOKS = ("setup", "teardown")` is matched with `name.lower().startswith(_HOOKS)`.
- Functions are keyed by bare name: module-level functions and every class's methods share one `units` table. So an uncalled module-level `go()` is credited when a test calls a method of the same name through `self.go()`, and a `test_*` method of a class that is not a test class, and that nothing makes, is credited too.
- A module-level helper handed on by reference (`anyio.run(go)`, `monkeypatch.setattr(x, "y", go)`) is not credited, though a nested one is.

Change experience/tool_matrix.py so that:
(1) A hook is a root only when its name is exactly one that pytest itself runs: at module level setup_module, teardown_module, setup_function and teardown_function; in a collected test class setup_class, teardown_class, setup_method and teardown_method; and unittest's setUp, tearDown, setUpClass and tearDownClass in a TestCase class, and setUpModule and tearDownModule at module level. Names are matched exactly, not by prefix and not case-folded. The nose-style plain setup and teardown are not run by pytest 8 or later, and this repository is on pytest 9. A helper called setup_shop or teardown_all runs only when running code reaches it.
(2) A name is resolved by where it is defined. A bare call or bare name reaches a module-level function or class of the file (or a nested one, as now). `self.x()` or `cls.x()` reaches the method x of the class the calling method is defined in, or of a base class of the same file that it names. It never reaches a module-level function called x, nor a method x of an unrelated class. A `test_*` method is a root only in a class pytest collects: one whose name starts with Test and that defines no __init__ (this repository sets no other python_classes), or one deriving from unittest.TestCase or TestCase. A `test_*` method of any other class runs only once running code makes that class, which is the existing model-double rule.
(3) A module-level function or class of the file that running code names without calling it (hands it to a call, returns it, assigns it or puts it in a container) is reached, as a nested one is now. The file's top-level code naming it still reaches nothing (the 2026-10-01 F-02 rule).
The module docstring, `_calls_that_run`'s docstring and the comment above the hook names say these rules.

Must not change: every existing case in tests/test_followups_harness.py and tests/test_tool_matrix.py, which keep passing unchanged (nested helpers, lambdas kept under a name, nested classes, model doubles, fixtures and autouse fixtures, top-level code, constants, the scenario rules); what counts as running a tool (dispatch, registry.invoke, the provider's callback, the handler by name); the scenario and GOLDEN SCENARIO columns (`scenario_strings`, `_scenario_tools`); every other column; and the rule that nothing is imported or run. Prove the change with new tests in crooks-assistant/tests/test_tool_audit_edges.py that ask tool_matrix.read_test(textwrap.dedent(source)).calls_tool('probe_tool', 'app.tools.probes', 'probe_tool'), the way tests/test_followups_harness.py's `_cites` asks. docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md is regenerated by the loop after you report (config/generated_files.json): do not edit it. Because your own check run comes before that regeneration, the regression check deselects tests/test_tool_matrix.py::test_the_checked_in_document_is_the_generated_one; GitHub acceptance runs it on the regenerated candidate. In your report, name any test file whose citation you expect to appear or disappear because of rules (1) to (3). Run every declared check yourself with the run_checks tool, exactly as declared, before you report, and report only a candidate on which all of them pass. If a check fails on the untouched base, report that base failure and its output instead of changing anything to hide it. You cannot delete files or run commands other than the declared checks. Do not report an owner decision for GitHub acceptance: it runs automatically on your published candidate.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch inside a module-level helper named setup_shop, teardown_all, setupThing or Setup_x that no test reaches is not cited; the same dispatch inside a real hook is cited: module-level setup_module, teardown_module, setup_function and teardown_function; setup_method, teardown_method, setup_class and teardown_class of a Test class; setUp, tearDown, setUpClass and tearDownClass of a unittest.TestCase subclass; and module-level setUpModule and tearDownModule (check: tests).

A module-level `async def go()` that dispatches is not cited when the only call is `await self.go()` in a test method of a Test class that defines its own non-dispatching `go`; a Test class's own dispatching `go` reached through `self.go()` is cited; and a module-level `go` called as `await go()` from a test method is cited (check: tests).

A `test_*` method that dispatches, in a class that is neither Test-prefixed nor a TestCase subclass and that nothing makes, is not cited; the same class made by running code (a fixture a test asks for returns it) is cited; a Test-prefixed class that defines __init__ is not collected, so its test_* methods are not roots (check: tests).

A module-level dispatching helper handed on by name from running code is cited: `anyio.run(go)` in a test, `monkeypatch.setattr(provider, "step", go)` in a test, and `return go` from a fixture a test asks for. Named only by the file's top-level code (`anyio.run(go)` at module level), it is not cited (check: tests).

Every existing test in tests/test_followups_harness.py and tests/test_tool_matrix.py passes unchanged, including test_the_matrix_does_not_cite_a_test_that_only_looks_tools_up (shopify_find_order is cited by tests/test_shopify_tools.py and not by tests/test_digest_relate.py) (check: regression).
Neither test file named above changes, docs/phase4/TOOL_MATRIX.md is not edited by the builder, and no column other than the test citations changes meaning; the docstrings state rules (1) to (3).
ruff passes on app, config, scripts, tests and experience/tool_matrix.py (check: ruff).
